blocks.title: LightCraft in the activity panel
blocks.description: A catalog and a darkroom — the upstream LightCraft raw developer running inside Astravia, on your own machine, with the images you opened in the workspace.

showcase.user_prompt: Open LightCraft and turn the background of @assets/cover.png into a blue gradient.
showcase.assistant_reply: Cover loaded. Turning the background into a blue gradient now.

items.title: The real darkroom
items.description: The panel serves the official LightCraft web build byte for byte. Upstream's wasm and JavaScript are not patched; only two thin files of ours are added around them.

items.title: Open and export through the workspace
items.description: Opening uses the file selected in the Explorer, and exports are written back through Astravia instead of a downloads folder.

items.title: A large first download, once
items.description: The payload is about 70 MB — the editor, its raw pipeline and a CJK interface font. It is fetched once into the plugin's data directory and reused offline.

items.title: Driven from the conversation
items.description: Ask in chat and the panel carries it out: pointer and keyboard steps run inside the editor one after another, each one named on the canvas while it happens.

items.title: Install the plugin
items.description: Nothing else to install: no desktop app, no camera codec pack, no account.

items.title: Open the LightCraft tab and let it fetch
items.description: The first open downloads about 70 MB. The preparation screen reports progress; later opens start from cache.

items.title: Select an image, then open it
items.description: File → Open inside the editor takes the file selected in Astravia rather than a system dialog.

items.title: Export back through the workspace
items.description: Developed output travels the same bridge as a save, so it lands where you chose.

blocks.content: The first open is a 70 MB download and the wasm module is large; on a slow connection expect a visible wait before the editor appears. This is the upstream build, not an extra package of ours.
Interface language: the editor itself is English only — upstream ships no other language. The tab shell, the preparation page and this page follow your Astravia language.

Automation is an ordinary operation, not a macro player: a batch is a list of pointer and key steps the editor receives exactly as if they came from a hand, paced by frames so a press lasts a press. The canvas reports a text map and its average colour back, which is how the agent checks that a change really happened before reporting it.
